answer: The first century in which Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends (Decoration increasing significantly while Form declines simultaneously) is the 17th century BCE — i.e. the BCE 1700 bin of capital.csv (covering 1700–1601 BCE under the upper-edge convention). Over the boundary from the BCE 1800 bin (Late Neolithic) to the BCE 1700 bin (Older Bronze Age), Pottery Decoration rises by +1.45σ (Zkeverz: -0.48 -> +0.97) while Pottery Form falls by -1.87σ (ZKeform: +0.74 -> -1.13). This is the UNIQUE opposite-sign transition in the entire BCE 4300..500 range and the first (chronologically oldest) such transition; it satisfies the chosen "significantly" criterion at every sensitivity threshold tested (τ ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50}σ) and remains the "first" boundary under ±1-year bin-alignment sensitivity.

payload.workflow: 1) Plan-stage inspection (artifacts/plan_inspection.py): confirmed schema (PotteryForm/PotteryForm_inter/PotteryDecoration/PotteryDecoration_inter in time_series_data.csv; BCE/ZKeform/Zkeverz in capital.csv), row counts (3601 annual; 39 centennial), ranges (CE -4100..-500; BCE 4300..500), and that time_series raw values reproduce capital.csv exactly at all 37 aligned years. 2) Main analysis (artifacts/main_analysis.py): primary scan on capital.csv oldest->youngest over 38 consecutive 100y bins computes Δ = newer_bin - older_bin for both series and flags transitions with ΔDecoration>0 and ΔForm<0 at |Δ|>0.10σ (sensitivity 0.05/0.25/0.50). Exactly one boundary qualifies, BCE 1800 -> BCE 1700 (ΔDec=+1.450σ, ΔForm=-1.870σ). 3) Cross-check: sampling time_series_data.csv Pottery*_inter at the upper-edge year (CE=-BCE) of each capital.csv row reproduces 37/37 mappable rows within 1e-6 (the two oldest capital rows BCE 4300/4200 pre-date the CE=-4100 floor of time_series_data.csv). ±1-year cross-check offsets also yield the same first century (BCE 1700).
